question: Why should nurses treat a patient's fear as a serious clinical issue?

options.A: It allows the nurse to discharge the patient much faster.
options.B: It removes the need to administer prescribed medications.
options.C: It helps the nurse deliver targeted and empathetic interventions.
options.D: It ensures the patient will never ask questions about surgery.

explanation: You got it! Acknowledging fear as a real medical concern lets us give patients the exact emotional and physical backup they need to heal. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T11#GNS123_U3_T11_h1)

question: Why do public health campaigns often focus mass deworming programs on school-aged children?

options.A: Children have the highest worm burdens and engage in behaviors that spread eggs
options.B: Adults are completely immune to reinfection after adolescence
options.C: Deworming tablets are only approved by regulators for pediatric use
options.D: Children are the only population that can develop lung complications

explanation: Kids play outside in the soil and tend to carry the highest number of worms, making school deworming programs super effective. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T22#GNS313_U2_T22_h6)

question: What is the main goal of conducting a financial audit in a hospital?

options.A: To punish individual bedside nurses for making minor clinical charting errors
options.B: To eliminate all patient care expenses across every hospital department
options.C: To verify the accuracy of financial records and ensure compliance with standards
options.D: To decide which physicians receive bonuses at the end of each month

explanation: Audits aren't witch hunts—they are routine checks to make sure financial records are honest, accurate, and following the rules. [learn more](GST321_U1_T24#GST321_U1_T24_h6)

question: When can palliative care start for someone diagnosed with cancer?

options.A: At the time of diagnosis alongside curative treatment
options.B: Only when all chemotherapy and radiation have failed
options.C: Strictly during the final twenty-four hours of life
options.D: Only after the patient is discharged to hospice care

explanation: Palliative care isn't just for the end of life—it can start right away to help manage symptoms and keep the patient comfortable while fighting the disease. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T15#GNS324_U4_T15_h8)

question: What is the main purpose of a commodity stock card in a family planning clinic?

options.A: To record the personal phone numbers of clients
options.B: To monitor inventory levels and prevent stockouts
options.C: To document detailed clinical side effects of pills
options.D: To evaluate the nursing staff's daily performance

explanation: Stock cards track the receipt and dispensing of contraceptive supplies to ensure the clinic never runs out unexpectedly. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T026#GNS226_U6_T026_h3)

question: A medical ward suddenly gets lots of new patients needing extra IV cannulas and dressings. Which budget item will go up?

options.A: Capital expenditure
options.B: Overhead revenue
options.C: Fixed costs
options.D: Variable costs

explanation: Spot on! Supplies like cannulas and dressings go up and down directly with patient volume, making them classic variable costs. [learn more](GST321_U4_T3#GST321_U4_T3_h3)

question: A primary health clinic in a rural Nigerian community wants to improve antenatal care attendance. What is the best first step based on local health system realities?

options.A: Report all pregnant women who miss clinic dates to the police
options.B: Consult village development committees and local women leaders
options.C: Close the clinic until pregnant women start coming on their own
options.D: Wait for federal funds to build a brand new modern hospital

explanation: Engaging trusted local structures helps identify why women are not attending and builds culturally acceptable solutions. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T4#GNS124_U4_T4_h3)

question: What blood pressure reading is used as the standard threshold to diagnose hypertension in pregnancy?

options.A: 130/85 mmHg or higher
options.B: 120/80 mmHg or higher
options.C: 160/100 mmHg or higher
options.D: 140/90 mmHg or higher

explanation: A reading of 140/90 mmHg or higher, confirmed on two separate occasions, defines pregnancy-induced hypertension. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T019#GNS226_U2_T019_h1)

question: A 45-year-old Nigerian civil servant works a desk job and has central obesity. Which condition is he most at risk for?

options.A: Acute diabetic ketoacidosis
options.B: Gestational diabetes
options.C: Type 1 autoimmune diabetes
options.D: Type 2 diabetes mellitus

explanation: Sitting for long hours, lack of exercise, and belly fat are classic risk factors for Type 2 diabetes. Seeing how this connects to real life makes clinical rotations much easier! [learn more](GNS313_U3_T3#GNS313_U3_T3_h4)

question: Why is it important to ask patients if they have visited patent medicine vendors when taking their history?

options.A: Hospital records automatically track all purchases made in private shops
options.B: Many informal vendors administer unsterile injections that patients forget to mention
options.C: Patent medicine vendors are legally required to report side effects
options.D: Patients only get infections when visiting registered general hospitals

explanation: Patients often think of informal drug purchases as casual and might forget to mention them. Asking directly helps us catch hidden risks like unsterile shots! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T4#GNS122_U3_T4_h6)

question: Why do droplet precautions only need a regular surgical mask instead of an N95?

options.A: Droplets are heavy, travel short distances, and do not linger in the air
options.B: Droplets evaporate instantly before reaching any healthcare worker
options.C: Droplets can only pass through skin pores, not through cloth
options.D: Surgical masks filter out microscopic floating particles better than N95s

explanation: Exactly! Large droplets quickly drop down rather than floating, so a simple surgical mask gives you all the protection you need for close care. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T4#GNS313_U2_T4_h3)

question: Your patient starts having trouble breathing and facial swelling right after a new IV antibiotic starts. What should you do first?

options.A: Stop the infusion immediately and notify the doctor.
options.B: Give the patient a glass of water and tell them to rest.
options.C: Write an incident report for the pharmacy department.
options.D: Slow down the drip rate and wait to see if it stops.

explanation: Patient safety first! Always stop the offending drug right away to prevent things from getting worse before calling the doctor. [learn more](GNS125_U5_T8#GNS125_U5_T8_h4)

question: Why is regular cleaning and disinfecting of bed accessories so important in the ward?

options.A: To keep the equipment looking brand new for visitors
options.B: To make the rubber and plastic components softer
options.C: To prevent the metal parts from rusting too quickly
options.D: To prevent the spread of hospital-acquired infections

explanation: Spot on! Since bed accessories are often shared, wiping them down thoroughly between patients stops germs from spreading and keeps everyone safe. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T4#GNS112_U4_T4_h6)

question: A nurse notices that a sterile instrument pack has a small water stain on the outside wrapper. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Open the pack and check if the metal tools feel wet inside
options.B: Use the instruments immediately before the stain gets larger
options.C: Wipe the outer wrapper with alcohol and store it back
options.D: Consider the pack contaminated and send it for re-sterilization

explanation: Moisture compromises the porous paper barrier, allowing bacteria to wick inside and contaminate the contents. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T68#GNS214_U1_T68_h5)

question: If you want to know everything a hospitalized patient ate over the past 24 hours, which tool should you use?

options.A: A 24-hour dietary recall
options.B: A complete blood cell count
options.C: A mid-upper arm tape measure
options.D: A serum lipid profile test

explanation: Correct! A 24-hour dietary recall simply has the patient walk you through every single food and drink they had since yesterday. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T002#GNS227_U2_T002_h7)

question: Why do nurses encourage residents to do parts of their daily care on their own?

options.A: To test whether the resident is trying to escape from the facility
options.B: To comply with legal mandates that forbid nurses from assisting with bathing
options.C: To preserve resident dignity, maintain functional ability, and promote autonomy
options.D: To reduce the number of staff members needed on duty during night shifts

explanation: Brilliant! Encouraging self-care helps older adults stay active, independent, and proud of what they can still do. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T12#GNS324_U5_T12_h5)

question: What is the main job of the motor areas in the brain's cerebral cortex?

options.A: Interpreting sounds and spoken language
options.B: Storing long-term episodic memories
options.C: Controlling voluntary muscle movements
options.D: Processing visual images from the eyes

explanation: You've got this! The motor areas are specially designed to plan and make happen all the voluntary movements your body makes every day. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T10#GNS211_U3_T10_h1)

question: What happens when a research checklist turns your observations into simple checkmarks?

options.A: It turns descriptive notes into countable data for statistics
options.B: It automatically publishes the findings in a journal
options.C: It removes all potential errors from the research process
options.D: It changes qualitative research into a medical prescription

explanation: Tick marks make counting things super easy, which lets you run simple math and stats on your findings later. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T23#GNS224_U1_T23_h2)

question: Right after a multiple birth, which complication should a nurse monitor for most closely?

options.A: Gestational diabetes
options.B: Postpartum hemorrhage
options.C: Chronic hypertension
options.D: Hyperemesis gravidarum

explanation: You nailed it! Because the uterus worked overtime stretching for multiples, checking for heavy bleeding (due to poor contraction) is rule number one right after delivery. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T018#GNS226_U2_T018_h7)

question: Why is teaching workers about toxic gases important in factories and industrial sites?

options.A: It helps workers recognize hidden breathing hazards and use safety gear
options.B: It eliminates the need for any medical staff on site
options.C: It reduces the cost of electricity in factories
options.D: It guarantees that machinery will never break down

explanation: Many toxic gases are invisible. Educating workers helps them spot dangers early and protect themselves with proper ventilation and masks. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T6#GNS221_U3_T6_h8)

question: Why should family caregivers avoid overprotecting a visually impaired relative?

options.A: Overprotection can rob the patient of remaining independence and confidence
options.B: Hospitals require relatives to stay away during recovery
options.C: The patient's eyesight might deteriorate faster with too much help
options.D: Family members will run out of money if they help too much

explanation: Doing everything for a patient can make them feel helpless and depressed. Encouraging them to do what they can builds their confidence! [learn more](GNS324_U4_T8#GNS324_U4_T8_h8)

question: How does ionization affect a drug's movement through the body?

options.A: Charged molecules have a harder time crossing cell membranes
options.B: Ionization has no effect on how medicine moves
options.C: Ionization stops the drug from ever entering the blood
options.D: Charged molecules move much faster through fat layers

explanation: Cell membranes don't like charged particles. So, if a drug is ionized, it tends to get stuck wherever it currently is instead of crossing over easily. [learn more](GNS125_U5_T2#GNS125_U5_T2_h2)

question: What do we call a sudden, severe change in mental state where a patient becomes very confused and restless?

options.A: Chronic anemia
options.B: Stable hypertension
options.C: Mild osteoarthritis
options.D: Acute delirium

explanation: Delirium is a sudden, temporary state of confusion often seen in hospitalised patients. It puts them at risk of pulling out their IV lines or climbing out of bed unassisted. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T8#GNS122_U3_T8_h4)

question: Why do many rural families traditionally view having many children as a great benefit?

options.A: The government pays monthly stipends for large households
options.B: Children provide farm labor and security in old age
options.C: Larger households receive free agricultural land allotments
options.D: School fees are fully subsidized for families with five children

explanation: Spot on! In farming communities, children help out on the farm and support their parents as they grow older. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T004#GNS226_U6_T004_h3)

question: What is the primary purpose of a community health nursery?

options.A: Offering long-term inpatient medical treatment for sick infants
options.B: Providing formal primary education for children over ten years old
options.C: Serving as an overnight residential facility for orphans
options.D: Providing supervised care and early development support for young children

explanation: Nurseries are designed to care for infants and toddlers during the day, supporting their growth while parents are away. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T8#GNS225_U4_T8_h1)

question: Why do midwives always give iron and folic acid supplements during antenatal care?

options.A: To cure acute bacterial infections of the urinary tract
options.B: To prevent the sudden onset of postpartum hemorrhage after delivery
options.C: To prevent nutritional anemia caused by increased blood volume demands
options.D: To lower elevated blood sugar levels associated with gestational diabetes

explanation: Spot on! Pregnancy increases blood volume, so extra iron and folic acid help build enough red blood cells to keep mom healthy and strong. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T11#GNS225_U3_T11_h5)

question: What percentage range of an adolescent's daily calories should ideally come from carbohydrates?
explanation: Carbohydrates provide the primary fuel source for daily energy and should form the largest share of teen calorie intake. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T007#GNS227_U2_T007_h2)

question: Which temporary side effect is very common after taking misoprostol?

options.A: Complete temporary paralysis
options.B: High blood pressure requiring medication
options.C: Chills and low-grade fever
options.D: Severe permanent hair loss

explanation: You got it! Misoprostol frequently causes mild, temporary side effects like chills, nausea, or a slight fever. They pass quickly! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T011#GNS226_U5_T011_h5)

question: Medical asepsis is also commonly referred to by which term?

options.A: Sterile technique
options.B: Clean technique
options.C: Barrier protection
options.D: Surgical isolation

explanation: Medical asepsis focuses on reducing the number of microbes and is widely known as clean technique in daily nursing tasks. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T1#GNS311_U4_T1_h2)

question: A male relative insists on answering all health questions for an adult female patient. Which concept best explains this situation?

options.A: Genetic mutation
options.B: Power dynamics
options.C: Biological sex
options.D: Symptom etiology

explanation: Spot on! Unequal power dynamics at home often mean one person takes over and speaks for others during health visits. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T6#GNS312_U4_T6_h2)

question: How does water pollution directly hurt everyday communities?

options.A: By speeding up the natural flow of underground aquifers
options.B: By lowering the overall temperature of local rivers
options.C: By increasing the mineral content of drinking water
options.D: By making available water sources unsafe for daily use

explanation: You got it! When water is contaminated, families can no longer use it safely for drinking, cooking, or basic hygiene, posing an immediate health threat. [learn more](GST114_U6_T6#GST114_U6_T6_h1)

question: What is a very common emotional experience for patients facing the end of their lives?

options.A: Existential distress and questioning life meaning
options.B: An intense desire to run marathons
options.C: Complete indifference to surroundings and people
options.D: Sudden loss of all emotional feelings

explanation: You got it! Toward the end of life, it's completely normal for patients to look back, wonder about their life's purpose, and work through big deep questions. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T3#GNS321_U4_T3_h5)

question: Because of where the breathing centers are located in the brain, which vital sign must a nurse monitor most closely in pontine injuries?

options.A: Orthostatic blood pressure changes
options.B: Core body temperature fluctuations
options.C: Peripheral oxygen saturation trends
options.D: Respiratory rate and breathing pattern

explanation: Spot on! Since the pons helps control breathing rhythms, keeping a close eye on your patient's respiratory pattern can save their life. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T20#GNS211_U3_T20_h6)

question: How often should you check the circulation and nerves (neurovascular status) of a limb in skin traction?

options.A: Only once a day during the morning shift
options.B: Only when the patient complains of severe pain
options.C: Once every week until discharge
options.D: Every two to four hours

explanation: Checking frequently helps you catch circulation or nerve issues early before any permanent damage happens. You are learning to be a vigilant nurse! [learn more](GNS221_U1_T8#GNS221_U1_T8_h5)

question: What is the main purpose of tracheobronchial suctioning?

options.A: Removing secretions to keep the airway clear
options.B: Expanding collapsed lung alveoli directly
options.C: Measuring the exact lung capacity
options.D: Delivering high concentrations of oxygen

explanation: Suctioning is primarily performed to clear trapped mucus and fluids when a patient cannot cough them out independently. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T12#GNS212_U2_T12_h1)

question: Why is it important to test draft survey questions on a small group before the main study?

options.A: To force participants to agree with the researcher
options.B: To finish the research project much faster
options.C: To catch hidden mistakes and confusing wording
options.D: To make the final paper look longer and better

explanation: Pilot testing helps identify confusing questions and errors before you spend time and resources on the full study. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T21#GNS224_U1_T21_h4)

question: What is the immediate nursing action if a chemical splashes into a patient's eyes?

options.A: Wait for laboratory blood test results before touching the face
options.B: Cover the eyes tightly with dry gauze bandages without washing
options.C: Flush the eyes continuously with clean water for at least fifteen minutes
options.D: Apply concentrated acid neutralizer drops directly to the corneas

explanation: Spot on! Quick and long flushing with clean water washes the chemical away before it can permanently damage the cornea. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T13#GNS313_U3_T13_h5)

question: What is papilledema?

options.A: Tiny yellow deposits forming underneath the central macula
options.B: A permanent tear in the outer peripheral layers of the retina
options.C: Swelling of the optic disc due to increased intracranial pressure
options.D: A cloudy white film covering the front surface of the cornea

explanation: Papilledema involves swelling of the optic nerve head and blurred disc margins, indicating dangerous pressure buildup inside the skull. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T8#GNS221_U2_T8_h8)

question: Why is the membrane inside the lungs where gas exchange happens so incredibly thin?

options.A: To allow the lungs to stretch easily during inhalation
options.B: To reduce the overall weight of the thoracic organs
options.C: To prevent white blood cells from entering the alveoli
options.D: To allow fast and efficient diffusion of gases

explanation: Spot on! A super thin wall means oxygen and carbon dioxide can zip back and forth between your lungs and blood instantly. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T1#GNS213_U2_T1_h3)

question: Why is it risky to ignore signs of depression in a patient managing a blood disorder?

options.A: Depression automatically causes an immediate drop in haemoglobin levels
options.B: Patients with depression are legally barred from receiving blood transfusions
options.C: Sadness always leads to permanent physical paralysis if left unmanaged
options.D: Untreated depression can severely reduce treatment adherence and self-care

explanation: When patients feel hopeless, they might skip clinic visits or meds. Spotting depression early keeps them on track with their healing. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T4#GNS311_U2_T4_h3)

question: What is a common consequence of mental health stigma in many communities?

options.A: Government agencies automatically provide free housing for patients
options.B: Patients recover much faster without taking any medications
options.C: People hide their symptoms and delay seeking professional help
options.D: Traditional healers refuse to communicate with psychiatric nurses

explanation: Stigma creates shame and fear of discrimination, causing individuals and families to hide psychiatric symptoms instead of getting medical care. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T4#GNS314_U2_T4_h5)

question: Why must nurses follow strict legal boundaries when giving powerful medications?

options.A: Because the pharmacy department requires extra paperwork
options.B: Because these substances have a high risk of abuse and harm
options.C: To ensure that doctors do not prescribe any treatment
options.D: So that hospital management can monitor daily staffing

explanation: Strong medications carry serious risks like addiction or overdose, making strict rules necessary for patient safety. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T13#GNS122_U1_T13_h1)

question: Why must a nurse check a patient's heart rate before and after giving a sympathomimetic drug?

options.A: The drug directly lowers the heart rate to dangerous levels
options.B: These medications can also stimulate heart receptors and cause a fast pulse
options.C: Heart rate is the only accurate way to measure lung capacity
options.D: Patients with asthma always have a slow pulse rate at baseline

explanation: Even though these drugs target the lungs, they can sometimes sneak over and tickle heart receptors too, causing a fast pulse or palpitations. Always good to check! [learn more](GNS223_U2_T5#GNS223_U2_T5_h4)

question: Why do doctors perform a colposcopy and take a biopsy after a woman gets an abnormal Pap smear result?

options.A: To clean out the entire uterine cavity and prevent future infections
options.B: To examine suspicious areas closely and take a tissue sample for definitive diagnosis
options.C: To measure the exact hormone levels circulating in the pelvic blood vessels
options.D: To instantly cure the viral infection using high-intensity light beams

explanation: Think of a Pap smear as a warning bell, while a colposcopy and biopsy are the detectives that look closer to confirm what is really going on. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T18#GNS216_U5_T18_h5)

question: What is the main test used to diagnose structural heart valve problems?

options.A: Echocardiogram
options.B: Routine head CT scan
options.C: Standard skin biopsy
options.D: Abdominal ultrasound

explanation: An echo is an ultrasound of the heart! It lets doctors actually see the heart valves moving and check how well blood is flowing. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T5#GNS213_U1_T5_h7)

question: What ethical action must nurse researchers take if an intervention being tested in a prospective trial proves to be significantly harmful?

options.A: Ask participants to sign a waiver accepting the new dangers
options.B: Hide the adverse results until the final academic paper is published
options.C: Continue the trial until the originally scheduled end date anyway
options.D: Stop the trial immediately to protect participants from further harm

explanation: Researcher safety oversight demands that patient welfare always supersedes study completion if unexpected dangers emerge. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T15#GNS224_U1_T15_h6)

question: Why is a working transport and referral system so important for saving mothers?

options.A: It lowers the cost of private maternity hospitals
options.B: It eliminates the need for trained midwives at primary health centers
options.C: It bridges the gap between remote communities and emergency obstetric facilities
options.D: It removes the need for antenatal clinics in rural areas

explanation: Getting transport right solves the 'second delay'—ensuring a woman in a village can actually reach a surgeon at a general hospital before it's too late. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T012#GNS226_U1_T012_h8)

question: What instruction should a nurse give a patient right after placing a sublingual tablet?

options.A: Drink a full glass of water immediately to wash it down.
options.B: Lie flat on your back for at least one hour.
options.C: Do not eat, drink, or smoke until the pill is fully dissolved.
options.D: Chew the tablet quickly to help it enter the bloodstream.

explanation: Eating or drinking washes the medication away before it can absorb through the oral mucosa. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T17#GNS125_U3_T17_h7)

question: What does the letter 'E' stand for in the health acronym IEC?

options.A: Evaluation
options.B: Environment
options.C: Education
options.D: Emergency

explanation: IEC stands for Information, Education, and Communication, which are core components of public health promotion strategies. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T4#GNS124_U5_T4_h1)

question: A nurse leader wants to assess the prevalence of needle-stick injuries among nurses in a state hospital to justify safety equipment purchases. Which study design is most appropriate?

options.A: Cross-sectional study
options.B: Case report of a single patient
options.C: Laboratory experiment on bacteria cultures
options.D: Retrospective drug trial over ten years

explanation: Spot on! A cross-sectional survey will quickly reveal how common needle-stick injuries are right now, giving solid proof to demand better safety gear. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T10#GNS224_U1_T10_h9)

question: Why is an MRI generally considered safer than a CT scan regarding radiation?

options.A: It exposes the body to much lower doses of standard X-rays
options.B: It completely avoids interacting with any atoms inside the human body
options.C: It requires the patient to take a protective oral medication first
options.D: It uses radiofrequency and magnetic fields instead of ionizing radiation

explanation: Spot on! Because an MRI doesn't use ionizing radiation, it's a much safer choice for avoiding radiation exposure. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T7#GNS222_U1_T7_h1)

question: What is the ultimate aim of a community health nurse in mobilisation?

options.A: Building local capacity so the community runs its own health programs
options.B: Collecting data to publish research papers in medical journals
options.C: Making sure the local clinic receives a large budget from abroad
options.D: Ensuring the nurse becomes the most respected person in the village

explanation: The goal of community mobilisation is self-reliance, where locals have the skills to manage their health without constant outside intervention. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T6#GNS124_U4_T6_h8)

question: How does applying knowledge of community structure change the way you deliver healthcare?

options.A: It shifts care from something imposed on people to a collaborative partnership
options.B: It removes the need for community health clinics in rural areas
options.C: It replaces professional nurses with traditional birth attendants completely
options.D: It forces patients to obey hospital rules without asking questions

explanation: You aren't just bossing people around; you are teaming up with them! Understanding the community turns healthcare delivery into a wonderful partnership built on trust. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T1#GNS124_U2_T1_h8)

question: What is the main goal of nursing inquiry?

options.A: To systematically search for knowledge relevant to practice
options.B: To write hospital policies without clinical input
options.C: To punish nurses who make clinical mistakes
options.D: To reduce the number of hospital admissions

explanation: Nursing inquiry is all about finding reliable knowledge to improve how we care for patients, teach, and run hospitals. You'll see this come up often in practice! [learn more](GNS217_U1_T2#GNS217_U1_T2_h1)

question: A nurse notices that teenagers avoid the clinic because staff members gossip. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Report all visiting teenagers to local religious leaders
options.B: Refuse to treat anyone under the age of eighteen
options.C: Train staff on confidentiality and non-judgmental attitudes
options.D: Close the adolescent clinic and open an adult-only wing

explanation: Exactly right! Building trust through strict confidentiality and a welcoming, non-judgmental attitude is key to helping teens feel safe at the clinic. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T11#GNS312_U3_T11_h8)

question: What happens to your pupil when you walk from a dark room into bright sunlight?

options.A: It turns completely white and opaque
options.B: It constricts to let less light enter
options.C: It flattens out against the cornea
options.D: It dilates to capture more light rays

explanation: Your pupil shrinks (constricts) in bright light to protect your eyes from getting overloaded. Easy peasy! [learn more](GNS211_U4_T6#GNS211_U4_T6_h3)

question: What standard manual do mental health professionals use to classify mental disorders?

options.A: Nursing Interventions Classification Handbook
options.B: International Directory of Psychiatric Medications
options.C: Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders
options.D: Standard Medical Treatment Guidelines for Africa

explanation: You'll hear this called the DSM! It's the standard guidebook clinicians use around the world to properly diagnose and categorize mental health conditions. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T2#GNS314_U1_T2_h2)

question: Which common medication class is one of the top triggers for hospital-acquired anaphylaxis?

options.A: Antihypertensive drugs
options.B: Inhaled bronchodilators
options.C: Penicillin antibiotics
options.D: Potassium supplements

explanation: Penicillin and other beta-lactam drugs are famous culprits. Always double-check a patient's allergy history before giving them! [learn more](GST114_U4_T9#GST114_U4_T9_h2)

question: What key element is missing from a vague aim statement like 'we will improve patient safety'?

options.A: Detailed medical diagnoses for every patient
options.B: A complete history of past nursing errors
options.C: The signatures of the hospital board of directors
options.D: Specific targets, a timeline, and the target patient group

explanation: You're getting the hang of it! Without knowing how much change, by when, and for whom, a team can't measure success. [learn more](GST319_U2_T8#GST319_U2_T8_h3)

question: A patient is very anxious about tests for a suspected adrenal tumor. What is the best initial nursing action?

options.A: Tell the patient to refuse all invasive tests until they feel calmer
options.B: Provide clear, simple explanations of the tests and offer emotional support
options.C: Administer a strong sedative without a doctor's prescription
options.D: Reassure the patient that adrenal tumors are never cancerous

explanation: You're a natural! Clear, compassionate communication and emotional support go a long way in calming patient fears and helping them through tests. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T4#GNS222_U2_T4_h8)

question: Why does a cut or break in the skin raise a patient's risk of getting sick?

explanation: Never skip this! Pulling out a catheter while the balloon is still full will cause severe, painful injury to the patient. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T21#GNS212_U1_T21_h9)

question: In community health, what do we mean by a non-human reservoir?

options.A: A medical facility designated strictly for treating infectious tropical diseases
options.B: A living or environmental source where a pathogen normally lives and multiplies
options.C: A pharmaceutical storage unit used to keep vaccines at very cold temperatures
options.D: A human patient who shows no active symptoms of a communicable illness

explanation: You've got this! Germs rely on reservoirs to survive and multiply in nature before they ever reach humans. Think of it as their permanent home base. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T6#GNS313_U2_T6_h1)

question: Primary hypertension is also frequently called what?

options.A: Secondary hypertension
options.B: Gestational hypertension
options.C: Reversible hypertension
options.D: Essential hypertension

explanation: We call it 'essential hypertension' when high blood pressure happens on its own without another clear medical condition causing it. Easy peasy! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T14#GNS214_U1_T14_h2)

question: A Muslim patient admitted during Ramadan needs medication three times a day with food. What should you do first?

options.A: Withhold all medications until the holy month of Ramadhan ends
options.B: Crush the medication and mix it into the patient's intravenous fluids
options.C: Insist that the patient break their religious fast immediately to take the pills
options.D: Collaborate with the care team to adjust medication timings around the fasting schedule

explanation: Teamwork makes the dream work! Always talk with the doctor and pharmacist to safely schedule meds for non-fasting hours during Ramadan whenever possible. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T019#GNS227_U2_T019_h3)

question: What helpful role do the resident bacteria in your colon play?

options.A: Digesting the majority of dietary fats and proteins
options.B: Producing protective mucus for the rectal lining
options.C: Synthesizing certain vitamins and fermenting fiber
options.D: Preventing all water absorption to keep stool soft

explanation: Correct! Our gut bacteria are friendly helpers that break down fiber and even manufacture important nutrients like vitamin K for us. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T1#GNS213_U3_T1_h6)

question: What was the original main goal of introducing Universal Precautions?

options.A: Ensuring accurate diagnosis of chronic illnesses
options.B: Speeding up the admission process for new patients
options.C: Protecting health workers from bloodborne pathogens
options.D: Lowering the overall cost of hospital equipment

explanation: Universal Precautions were originally created specifically to shield healthcare staff from infections transmitted through blood and specific body fluids. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T8#GNS313_U2_T8_h1)

question: What are the two best ways to identify a patient before giving them medication?

options.A: Checking the ID band and asking their name and date of birth
options.B: Looking at the room number and asking the hospital cleaner
options.C: Checking the chart stored outside on the nurses' station desk
options.D: Recognizing their face from walking past their bed yesterday

explanation: Always use two unique identifiers—like checking their wristband and asking them to speak their name and DOB—to keep medication mix-ups away. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T1#GNS125_U3_T1_h5)

question: What is the main job of hepatocytes inside the liver?

options.A: Producing red blood cells
options.B: Handling metabolism and clearing out toxins
options.C: Pumping oxygenated blood into the systemic circulation
options.D: Filtering waste through the kidneys

explanation: Hepatocytes are the hardworking main cells of the liver. They manage your metabolism, build proteins, and clear out body toxins every single day! [learn more](GNS222_U2_T5#GNS222_U2_T5_h1)

question: When would a nurse manager rely on a single-use plan?

options.A: When enforcing standard hand hygiene protocols
options.B: When writing the daily morning shift assignment
options.C: When managing a unique, one-time project or emergency event
options.D: When following routine hospital admission guidelines

explanation: Single-use plans are built for specific, non-recurring events and are discarded or archived once the project or event concludes. [learn more](GST321_U1_T6#GST321_U1_T6_h5)

question: What is the primary purpose of community entry in the mobilisation cycle?

options.A: Collecting taxes from local market traders
options.B: Building a permanent health clinic building
options.C: Conducting mass vaccinations for all children
options.D: Gaining social and legal acceptance from local leaders

explanation: Community entry is all about introducing yourself, getting permission, and building trust with local leaders before starting any work. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T6#GNS124_U4_T6_h3)

question: A patient suffers a stroke in the left motor cortex of the brain. Where will the resulting muscle weakness appear?

options.A: Only in the muscles of the face
options.B: On the right side of the body
options.C: Equally on both sides of the body
options.D: On the left side of the body

explanation: Because motor fibers cross at the medullary pyramids, damage to one side of the brain affects the contralateral side of the body. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T21#GNS211_U3_T21_h3)

question: What is a major challenge for nursing students facing heavy financial stress?

options.A: Elimination of the need to purchase nursing textbooks
options.B: An immediate increase in clinical ward placement scores
options.C: Free access to high-end medical simulation software
options.D: Balancing exhausting work schedules with studies, leaving little time for rest

explanation: Financial pressure often forces students to hustle outside of school, cutting deeply into study and recovery time. Hang in there—balancing nursing school is no small feat! [learn more](GST321_U8_T9#GST321_U8_T9_h4)

question: What is the main reason to teach an osteoarthritis patient about 'activity pacing'?

options.A: To ensure the patient finishes all chores before morning stiffness starts
options.B: To eliminate all physical movement from their daily routine
options.C: To balance rest periods with tasks and protect joints from overuse
options.D: To prevent the need for any future medical evaluations

explanation: Correct! Pacing helps patients get their daily tasks done without pushing their joints too hard and causing extra pain. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T13#GNS222_U1_T13_h8)

question: What is the main difference between hygiene factors and motivators in Herzberg's theory?

options.A: Motivators are about physical health, while hygiene factors are about pay
options.B: Hygiene factors apply only to doctors, while motivators apply to nurses
options.C: Hygiene factors prevent dissatisfaction, while motivators drive true engagement
options.D: Hygiene factors guarantee promotion, while motivators prevent illness

explanation: Good pay and working conditions stop us from complaining (hygiene), but doing meaningful work is what truly makes us love the job (motivators). [learn more](GST321_U3_T7#GST321_U3_T7_h2)

question: Why does a birth attendant massage the mother's uterus gently after the placenta is delivered?

options.A: To help the mother expel remaining amniotic fluid
options.B: To encourage uterine contraction and prevent heavy bleeding
options.C: To stimulate milk production in the breasts
options.D: To reposition the internal organs properly

explanation: Uterine massage compresses open blood vessels at the placental site, which is the primary defense against postpartum hemorrhage. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T10#GNS225_U2_T10_h6)

question: How can community nurses best help parents prevent accidental poisoning in toddlers?

options.A: Advising families to transfer all cleaning chemicals into empty soda bottles
options.B: Recommending that households avoid buying any chemical products entirely
options.C: Encouraging parents to induce vomiting in children at the first sign of illness
options.D: Teaching parents to store medications and cleaning agents in locked cabinets out of reach

explanation: Prevention is key! Keeping dangerous items locked away out of a toddler's curious reach is the best way to keep them safe. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T14#GNS221_U3_T14_h7)

question: Which category of substances acts by slowing down brain activity and central nervous system functions?

options.A: Stimulants
options.B: Hallucinogens
options.C: Inhalants
options.D: Depressants

explanation: Correct! Depressants like alcohol put the brakes on the nervous system, which can dangerously lower breathing and heart rates if taken in excess. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T4#GNS313_U3_T4_h2)

question: Why must a nurse check many different body systems when looking out for endocrine disorders?

options.A: Because hormone levels never fluctuate throughout a normal twenty-four-hour day
options.B: Because hormones circulate widely and influence multiple organs and metabolic processes
options.C: Because endocrine glands are all located together in the lower abdominal cavity
options.D: Because nervous system reflexes instantly replace any missing hormone functions

explanation: Hormones travel through the bloodstream touching many organs at once, which is why a single hormone imbalance can cause symptoms all over the body! [learn more](GNS222_U2_T1#GNS222_U2_T1_h8)

question: What are the common signs of Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia in someone with advanced HIV?

options.A: Severe throat pain and difficulty swallowing
options.B: Sudden chest pain and sharp pleuritic discomfort
options.C: Progressive dry cough and shortness of breath
options.D: Productive cough with rust-colored sputum

explanation: This opportunistic infection usually starts slowly with a dry cough, low fever, and trouble breathing during activity. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T13#GNS216_U6_T13_h2)

question: What document tells medical staff that a patient does not want lifesaving measures like CPR?

options.A: Advanced directive or DNR order
options.B: Surgical consent waiver
options.C: Medical insurance policy
options.D: Hospital admission agreement

explanation: A DNR (Do Not Resuscitate) order or advance directive honors the patient's personal wishes regarding emergency medical interventions. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T7#GNS321_U2_T7_h7)

question: What makes a 'cytokine storm' so dangerous in severe COVID-19 patients?

options.A: It causes widespread tissue damage and multi-organ failure
options.B: It permanently blocks the absorption of oral medications
options.C: It causes a sudden and permanent drop in blood pressure only
options.D: It immediately destroys all white blood cells in the body

explanation: Spot on! A cytokine storm is like an immune system overdrive. It floods the body with inflammatory signals that end up harming healthy organs. Keep up the good work! [learn more](GNS123_U4_T6#GNS123_U4_T6_h1)

question: Which of these actions is WRONG when monitoring a client's nutritional progress?

options.A: Checking regular weight trends over time
options.B: Ignoring client feedback on food preferences
options.C: Documenting specific physical measurements
options.D: Reviewing the client's recent food diaries

explanation: Never ignore what the client likes! Diet plans only work if they fit the client's personal lifestyle and taste. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T002#GNS227_U3_T002_h7)

question: Why are waste handlers considered a high-risk group for unsafe injection practices?

options.A: They frequently handle poorly disposed sharp medical waste
options.B: They process expired oral medications in the pharmacy
options.C: They administer injections to community members at home
options.D: They clean hospital floors without wearing heavy boots

explanation: Waste handlers often encounter stray needles thrown into regular trash instead of puncture-proof safety boxes. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T5#GNS122_U3_T5_h4)

question: Why is plotting a child's measurements over time better than taking just a single measurement?

options.A: It is the only legal requirement for pediatric hospital admission
options.B: It reveals individual growth trends rather than just a one-time snapshot
options.C: It eliminates all possible errors made during the weighing process
options.D: It removes the need to use standard growth charts

explanation: Think of it like a movie versus a single photograph. One measurement only shows you right now, but tracking over time shows the real direction and speed of the child's development. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T005#GNS227_U2_T005_h1)

question: Why might an elderly patient with a severe bacterial infection not run a high fever?

options.A: Older adults naturally maintain a much higher internal baseline temperature
options.B: The aging immune system has a blunted inflammatory and febrile response
options.C: Lung tissue infections never trigger body temperature changes at any age
options.D: Circulating white blood cells destroy all heat-producing chemicals instantly

explanation: Brilliant! Because of immunosenescence, older bodies often fail to mount a classic high fever, even when fighting a dangerous infection. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T2#GNS321_U3_T2_h6)

question: If you absolutely must recap a used needle, what is the safest technique to use?

options.A: The one-handed scoop technique
options.B: Holding the cap tightly in the palm of your hand
options.C: Pushing the needle directly into the cap using both hands
options.D: Asking a colleague to hold the cap while you insert the needle

explanation: Brilliant! The one-handed scoop method keeps your free hand safely away from the sharp tip so you don't accidentally poke yourself. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T2#GNS122_U4_T2_h7)

question: Which of these is a major duty of a registered dietitian in a hospital?

options.A: Administering routine intravenous medications to patients
options.B: Prescribing medical nutrition therapy and assessing status
options.C: Ordering all diagnostic blood tests for the ward
options.D: Performing surgical procedures on the gastrointestinal tract

explanation: Exactly! Dietitians are the experts at evaluating a patient's nutritional health and designing specific therapeutic diets for recovery. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T002#GNS227_U4_T002_h3)

question: Why is the large surface area of the peritoneal cavity so useful in medical care?

options.A: It prevents any medication from entering the systemic bloodstream
options.B: It stores excess fat to protect organs from physical trauma
options.C: It completely stops bacteria from causing localized infections
options.D: It provides a wide space for efficient fluid and drug exchange

explanation: Exactly! Because the peritoneal membrane is so wide and full of tiny blood vessels, it acts like a giant sponge, making it easy to swap fluids and medicines in and out. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T11#GNS125_U3_T11_h2)

question: A patient post-abortion complains of sudden, sharp belly pain, and her abdomen feels very hard and stiff. What complication should come to mind?

options.A: Post-procedure anxiety
options.B: Mild urinary tract infection
options.C: Normal uterine cramping
options.D: Uterine perforation

question: When is the best time to talk about end-of-life wishes and care planning with the family?

options.A: As early in the disease trajectory as possible
options.B: When the patient develops sudden aspiration pneumonia
options.C: Immediately after the final post-mortem examination
options.D: Only after the patient becomes completely mute and bedbound

explanation: Having these conversations early lets the patient share what they want while they still can, making future medical choices much easier for everyone involved. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T6#GNS222_U4_T6_h7)

question: When a patient uses a single-point cane for walking, which hand should hold the cane?

options.A: The hand on the stronger side
options.B: The hand on the weaker side
options.C: Both hands must hold the handle
options.D: Whichever hand is most dominant

explanation: Holding the cane on the strong side allows the patient to lean weight onto it while moving the opposite weak leg forward. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T3#GNS324_U6_T3_h3)

question: Which agency in Nigeria is officially in charge of tracking drug safety and pharmacovigilance?

options.A: NAFDAC

options.D: NMA

explanation: Correct! NAFDAC regulates food and drugs in Nigeria and runs the National Pharmacovigilance Centre to keep watch on drug safety. [learn more](GNS215_U2_T1#GNS215_U2_T1_h5)

question: What is the medical term for the complete absence of menstrual periods?

options.A: Menorrhagia
options.B: Dysmenorrhea
options.C: Amenorrhea
options.D: Metrorrhagia

explanation: Amenorrhea simply means 'no menses.' It can be primary (if periods never started) or secondary (if regular periods stopped). [learn more](GNS121_U5_T6#GNS121_U5_T6_h8)

question: A patient on warfarin asks if they can take routine ibuprofen for joint pain. What should you tell them?

options.A: Only take ibuprofen if you crush the tablets into powder first
options.B: Substitute ibuprofen with local herbal mixtures to avoid side effects

options.D: Yes, ibuprofen is completely safe to combine with any blood-thinning medication

question: Why is emotional and psychological support so important in high-risk pregnancy care?

options.A: Patients on bed rest have nothing else to do during the day
options.B: Mental health counseling replaces the need for medical check-ups
options.C: Chronic stress and anxiety can negatively affect both maternal and fetal well-being
options.D: It guarantees the mother will have a natural vaginal delivery

explanation: Mind and body are connected! High stress releases hormones that can impact the pregnancy, so a comforting word from you as a nurse goes a long way. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T010#GNS226_U2_T010_h6)

question: When choosing a speculum size for an adult patient, what should you do?

options.A: Choose the largest size that fits comfortably into the ear canal

options.C: Avoid using a speculum and insert the metal otoscope head directly
options.D: Always use the smallest size available to prevent patient discomfort

explanation: A bigger speculum actually keeps you from accidentally poking the instrument in too deep, while giving you a much better view! [learn more](GNS221_U2_T3#GNS221_U2_T3_h3)

question: Why do doctors check for other issues like thyroid problems when evaluating someone for andropause?

options.A: Thyroid hormones directly destroy circulating testosterone

options.C: Hypothyroidism stops the testicles from producing sperm
options.D: Thyroid disease prevents sex hormone-binding globulin from working

explanation: Many conditions like thyroid issues cause the same tiredness and mood changes, so ruling them out helps us make sure it's really andropause. [learn more](GNS121_U4_T8#GNS121_U4_T8_h4)

question: A clinic ensures that all adolescents receive care regardless of their financial status or background. Which core principle does this practice demonstrate?

options.A: Acceptability
options.B: Appropriateness
options.C: Confidentiality
options.D: Equitability

explanation: Equitability means treating all young clients fairly without discrimination based on status, gender, or ability to pay. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T16#GNS312_U3_T16_h2)

question: What is the main goal of antenatal care (ANC) services for a pregnant mother?

options.A: Determine the exact sex of the baby early on
options.B: Eliminate all physical discomforts during gestation
options.C: Monitor normal pregnancy and detect early complications
options.D: Guarantee a completely pain-free labor experience

explanation: Spotting issues early is everything! ANC is all about watching how the pregnancy progresses so you can catch and manage any little problem before it becomes serious. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T008#GNS226_U1_T008_h1)

question: How does systems theory describe an organization like a hospital?

options.A: As a set of interconnected parts working together
options.B: As a strict government entity that cannot change
options.C: As a collection of completely independent workers
options.D: As a machine that never interacts with the outside world

explanation: Systems theory views organizations as living networks where inputs, processes, and outputs affect every department. [learn more](GST321_U1_T3#GST321_U1_T3_h5)

question: What do we call all the chemical reactions that happen inside the body?

options.A: Responsiveness
options.B: Homeostasis
options.C: Differentiation
options.D: Metabolism

explanation: Great job! Metabolism is just the word we use for all the building up and breaking down of substances happening inside your cells to keep you going. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T1#GNS111_U1_T1_h3)

question: Why is parent involvement essential in school health initiatives?

options.A: To pay salaries for the school health staff
options.B: To reinforce healthy behaviors at home
options.C: To take over daily nursing duties in class
options.D: To design the academic curriculum for the term

explanation: When parents support health lessons at home, children receive consistent messages that make healthy habits stick. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T1#GNS225_U4_T1_h8)

question: Which of these is NOT an ethical requirement during a health screening exercise?

options.A: Keeping client test results strictly confidential
options.B: Respecting the cultural beliefs of the client
options.C: Forcing clients to participate even if they refuse
options.D: Explaining the limitations of the screening test

question: Why is it risky for a nursing research project to lack clear objectives?

options.A: The study will easily lose direction and gather irrelevant data
options.B: The nursing staff will refuse to participate in the study
options.C: The sample size will become too large to calculate
options.D: The hospital ethics committee will automatically grant funding

explanation: Without clear targets, you might end up collecting a mountain of unnecessary information that doesn't actually solve your clinical problem. Good objectives keep you focused! [learn more](GNS217_U3_T9#GNS217_U3_T9_h1)

question: A study shows a link between carrying a cigarette lighter and getting lung cancer. What role does smoking tobacco play here?

options.A: It is a confounding or underlying variable connecting the two
options.B: It is a zero-correlation factor with no medical relevance
options.C: It is an experimental intervention created by the researcher
options.D: It is a statistical error made during data entry

explanation: You got it! Lighters don't cause cancer directly—smoking tobacco is the underlying habit driving both things. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T12#GNS224_U1_T12_h6)

question: What is the main danger when a patient stops taking her antibiotics halfway just because she feels better?

options.A: Surviving germs can multiply and cause drug resistance
options.B: The laboratory will lose the record of her initial test
options.C: The patient will instantly develop a severe viral illness
options.D: Her body will stop producing any natural red blood cells

question: How does triage during a mass casualty incident differ from everyday emergency department triage?

options.A: It completely ignores patients with bleeding wounds

options.C: It is performed exclusively by hospital administrators sitting in offices
options.D: It focuses on saving the greatest number with limited resources rather than treating everyone with maximum effort

explanation: In a mass casualty incident, the goal shifts to saving as many lives as possible using fast sorting methods, rather than spending all resources on one critical patient. Brilliant effort! [learn more](GNS315_U2_T1#GNS315_U2_T1_h6)

question: You are about to give a patient a drug with a dosage you aren't sure about. What should you do?

options.A: Check the formulary or drug guide to confirm the correct safe dosage range
options.B: Administer the medication immediately to avoid delaying ward routines
options.C: Throw the medication away in the clinical waste bin without telling anyone
options.D: Ask another patient in the same ward what dose they usually take

explanation: Always double-check! Consulting a trusted drug guide keeps your patient safe and builds your clinical confidence. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T5#GNS215_U1_T5_h6)

question: What is the primary job of an ascending spinal tract?

options.A: Carrying motor commands down to the muscles
options.B: Carrying sensory information up to the brain
options.C: Producing cerebrospinal fluid in the spinal canal
options.D: Anchoring the spinal cord to the vertebrae

question: Why do patients with Addison's disease (primary adrenal insufficiency) often develop dark, pigmented skin?

options.A: The adrenal glands leak excess stored pigments directly into the blood

options.C: Poor kidney function traps waste products underneath the skin layers
options.D: The pituitary gland releases high amounts of ACTH, which stimulates melanin

question: Which complaint from a patient is a classic warning sign of pelvic floor trouble?

options.D: Sudden numbness in the lower legs

question: Why should researchers be honest about study limitations in their published papers?

options.A: To trick reviewers into approving weak methodologies
options.B: To avoid paying taxes on research grants
options.C: To make the paper shorter and easier to read
options.D: To ensure readers interpret findings with appropriate caution

explanation: You nailed it! Total honesty about what a study *couldn't* do stops clinicians from misapplying the results on the wards. [learn more](GNS217_U2_T2#GNS217_U2_T2_h7)

question: What is the main job of an autoclave in medical waste processing?

options.A: Burning plastic waste into black ash
options.B: Using steam under pressure to sterilize items
options.C: Freezing biological tissues for transport
options.D: Crushing glass ampoules into fine powder

explanation: Spot on! Autoclaves use hot steam under pressure to kill germs on equipment, making them safe to handle or throw away. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T4#GNS122_U5_T4_h6)

question: How do unequal gender roles in a relationship usually affect a woman's reproductive choices?

options.A: She may lack the authority to decide on contraceptive use or family size
options.B: She automatically gains complete control over household finances
options.C: Extended family members lose all interest in her personal life
options.D: Her partner is legally required to consult her on all medical matters

explanation: You got it! In male-dominated settings, women often struggle to make independent choices about birth control. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T022#GNS226_U5_T022_h6)

question: What is cultural competence in nursing mainly about?

options.A: Convincing every client to abandon traditional home remedies
options.B: Speaking multiple foreign languages fluently before practicing
options.C: Treating every single patient using the exact same routine
options.D: Understanding and respecting diverse beliefs and health practices

explanation: Cultural competence involves recognizing and respecting cultural differences to provide safe, individualized nursing care. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T22#GNS225_U2_T22_h6)

question: Which muscle group makes up the main bulk of the pelvic floor?

options.A: Levator ani
options.B: Piriformis
options.C: Obturator internus
options.D: Gluteus maximus

explanation: You nailed it! The levator ani is the star player here—it forms the major muscular sling of the pelvis. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T11#GNS121_U5_T11_h2)

question: Why are day care centres particularly vulnerable to infectious disease outbreaks?

options.A: Clients live permanently inside the building
options.B: Groups of vulnerable individuals gather in close contact
options.C: Staff members are not allowed to wash their hands
options.D: Sanitation guidelines forbid the use of soap and water

explanation: Gathering young children or frail adults in enclosed spaces makes it easy for germs to spread rapidly among them. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T7#GNS225_U4_T7_h4)

question: What do we call the ongoing health issues that linger for months after recovering from initial COVID-19?

options.A: Post-infectious immunity
options.B: Secondary sepsis
options.C: Acute viral syndrome
options.D: Long COVID

explanation: Correct! 'Long COVID' is the term used when symptoms stick around long after the acute virus has cleared the body. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T6#GNS123_U4_T6_h8)

question: What long-term problem can happen to the urinary tract from severe scarring due to untreated infections?

options.A: Testicular hypertrophy

options.C: Enlarged prostate gland
options.D: Chronic kidney stones

question: Your patient has taken an expectorant for 10 days, but still has a bad cough, green phlegm, and a fever of 39°C. What should you do first?

options.A: Double the dose of the medication to speed up the healing process
options.B: Document that the medication cured the respiratory infection

question: Why are pregnant mums strongly advised to take folic acid supplements early on?

question: What causes an obstetric fistula when a young mother has a very long, difficult labor?
